quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Increase your following distance.
Decrease your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance to avoid collisions. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Stay flexible about your lane position.

questions.question: How should you stop a motorcycle normally?

options.text: Only the front brake should be used.
The front and rear brakes should be applied at the same time.
Only the rear brake should be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front and rear brakes should be applied at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a normal stop, use the front and rear brakes together at the same time and downshift.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Signal ahead.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Perform both actions at the same time.
Only brake.
Perform one action, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Perform one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do not brake and swerve at the same time. Instead, brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.

questions.question: How should a load be secured on a motorcycle?

options.text: Secured as low as possible.
Secured as high as possible.
Attached to a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Loads should be secured as low as possible, preferably in saddlebags. Attaching a load high on the motorcycle raises its center of gravity and affects balance.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT important for helmet protection?

options.text: U.S. DOT-compliant.
Loose-fitting.
Free of defects.

questions.correctAnswerText: Loose-fitting.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet DOT standards, fit snugly all the way around, and have no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. A loose-fitting helmet does not provide proper protection.

questions.question: What should you do when riding over grooved pavement in a work zone?

options.text: Look down to watch for changes in the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Move to the edge of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up in a work zone. Ride slowly over the grooved pavement.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance for a motorcycle under normal conditions?

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least a two-second distance from the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Use a larger distance if conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: What should you do if the front wheel locks while braking?

options.text: Release the front brake immediately, then re-apply the brake.
Release the front brake immediately and only use the rear brake.
Keep the front wheel locked until you come to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately, then re-apply the brake.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks while braking, release the brake right away and then re-apply it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black lettering alert you to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the right lane is ending ahead.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the signal is about to turn red. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, keep going.

questions.question: In the center of a traffic lane, there is usually an oily strip. Motorcyclists should:

options.text: Avoid riding on the oil and grease buildup.
Not worry about the oil and grease buildup.
Find the lane with the least oil and grease buildup.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid riding on the oil and grease buildup.
questions.explanation: Avoid riding on oil and grease buildup. This oily strip is usually only about two feet wide. You can ride to the left or right side of it and still stay in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: When carrying a load, it should be:

options.text: Secured as high as possible.
Secured as low as possible.
Secured on a sissy bar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep loads secured low to protect your motorcycle's balance.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
It automatically brakes based on your riding habits.
It applies the brake when you downshift gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems that link the front and rear brakes together when you apply the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual to learn about your specific motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: When positioning your body on the motorcycle:

options.text: You should hold yourself up with your arms.
Your arms should be used to steer the motorcycle.
You should have to stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your arms should be used to steer the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: For proper riding posture, position yourself so your arms steer the motorcycle, not hold you up. Sit so your elbows are slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: A difference between goggles and a windshield is:

options.text: Goggles protect you from the wind, but a windshield doesn't.
A windshield protects you from the wind, but goggles don't.
A windshield keeps your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect you from the wind, but a windshield doesn't.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from the wind, but most windshields do not. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: Before starting a turn, a motorcyclist should change gears to:

options.text: Prevent a power change in the middle of the turn.
Keep both hands on the handgrips during the turn.
Keep the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent a power change in the middle of the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start a turn. Shifting while turning can cause a sudden power change to the rear wheel and cause a skid. If you must shift during a turn, do it smoothly to prevent skidding.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while you are stopping on a straightaway:

options.text: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
You will likely lose control of the motorcycle.
You will need to release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can usually maintain control of the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straightaway, you can keep it locked until you stop. Even with a locked rear wheel, you can usually control your motorcycle if it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation recommends a SEE strategy for safe riding. What does "SEE" stand for?

options.text: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
Slow, Experienced, and Error-free.
Safe, Experienced, and Evasive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
questions.explanation: Experienced riders use the SEE strategy to make safe decisions. "SEE" stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcycle responds to directional changes:

options.text: More slowly than usual.
More quickly than usual.
Normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. With this added weight, your motorcycle will respond more slowly to your movements. It will take longer to speed up, slow down, and turn.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle, you:

options.text: May go 10 mph over the speed limit.
Must not exceed the speed limit.
Must ride faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must not exceed the speed limit.
questions.explanation: You must pass another vehicle within the posted speed limit. Only pass where it is safe and legal.

questions.question: While riding, you should wear:

options.text: Hearing protection to protect your hearing from engine and wind noise.
A helmet to protect your hearing.
A baseball cap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hearing protection to protect your hearing from engine and wind noise.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a full-face helmet. Wear hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: The oily strip down the center of a lane:

options.text: Should only be used if you are sharing the lane with another vehicle.
Usually gives good traction for riding, unless it is raining.
Should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually gives good traction for riding, unless it is raining.
questions.explanation: The center strip is usually oily but gives enough traction for safe riding, unless it is raining. The strip is usually about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center of the lane.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should:

options.text: Lead the group.
Be near the front of the group.
Be at the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be near the front of the group.
questions.explanation: Put less experienced riders near the front, right behind the leader. This lets experienced riders lead and watch the inexperienced riders at the same time.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, you should:

options.text: Keep the tire locked to stop more quickly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away and apply it again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it again.
questions.explanation: If the front wheel locks up while braking, release the front brake pressure immediately. Then reapply the brake with steady, gentle pressure.

questions.question: Making eye contact with another driver:

options.text: Means they see you.
Does not mean they will properly yield to you.
Guarantees they will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean they will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Never assume a driver will yield to you just because you make eye contact. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but still fail to see them.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: The outside of the curve
The inside of the curve
Wherever traffic and road conditions require

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever traffic and road conditions require
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that fits the conditions and change it as needed.

questions.question: If you accidentally lock your rear brake on a surface with good traction, you should:

options.text: Release the rear brake.
Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear tire on a surface with good traction, keep it locked until you stop completely. Your motorcycle will stay under control on good traction as long as it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Railroad crossing ahead
Yield
Reduce speed

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that a railroad crossing is coming up.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a factor in blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How quickly the alcohol is consumed
How often the person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: BAC depends on body weight, how much alcohol is consumed, and how quickly it is consumed. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.
